newsitem.title: CHINA: Cathay posts 35 percent drop in interim net.
newsitem.headline: Cathay posts 35 percent drop in interim net.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd posted a 35 percent drop in interim net profit Wednesday, with the grounding of its Airbus fleet, a slump in Japanese traffic and weak currencies dealing a blow to its performance.

The Hong Kong carrier said net profit dropped to HK$1.07 billion ($138 million) from HK$1.65 billion ($213 million) in the same 1996 period. The 1996 figure included an exceptional gain of HK$541.0 million ($69 million).
Turnover during the first six months of the year rose to HK$15.78 billion ($2.04 billion) compared with HK$15.16 billion ($1.96 billion).
"The first half of 1997 presented a series of difficult challenges for Cathay Pacific," chairman Peter Sutch said.
"Currency fluctuations, a weak summer travel market and the brief suspension of A330-300 operations created a number of obstacles for the airline," he said in a statement.
Cathay Pacific suspended service of its 11 A330-300s in late May after three inflight engine shutdowns on Cathay and a fourth on Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd. Service resumed by June 10.

Cathay Pacific said passenger load factors had declined substantially since May. "Overall revenue load factor was up slightly during the first half, averaging 71.2 percent, but downward pressure on yields and the weakness of certain European currencies reduced revenues on many routes," it said.

Cathay's net operating profit fell to HK$1.13 billion ($146 million) during the first half of the year from HK$1.17 billion ($151 million) in the 1996 period. It had no exceptional items compared with last year's gain on the sale of a 12.21 percent stake in Dragonair.
Analysts said there could be some weakness in Cathay shares on Thursday although investors had anticipated disappointing results. The stock fell HK$0.20 on Wednesday to HK$14.00 a share.
